title: Exhaust — Thrust Reverser Blocker Door Link Bushing Wear Inspection
abstract: Repeat inspection of the blocker door link bushings for ovality, covering the population between the current inspection interval and the opportunity to embody the self-lubricating bushing standard.

sections.planning_reason: Twelve operators reported reverser deployment times drifting apart between the two halves of a cowl, and inspection found the blocker door link bushings worn oval on the loaded flank at between four and six thousand cycles against a design life of twenty thousand. Two events produced a partially stowed blocker with the sleeve fully stowed, a condition the position sensing does not detect. The modification bulletin can only be embodied at reverser overhaul, so the fleet needs an inspection to bridge the interval.
sections.description: This is an inspection Service Bulletin. Each blocker door link bushing is measured for ovality with a bore gauge at two planes, and the aft seal is examined for the lip damage that admits fan-stream debris into the link housing. No parts are changed unless a measurement is outside limits, in which case the bushing and the seal are renewed as an interim measure.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the reverser halves in accordance with the maintenance manual and support them. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT THE REVERSER IS DEACTIVATED AND THE LOCKOUT IS INSTALLED BEFORE ANY PERSON WORKS INSIDE THE COWL. Do AMM-S-78-30-11-000-047-A to remove the blocker door links. Measure each bushing bore at two planes ninety degrees apart with the bore gauge and record both readings. Examine the aft seal D7830117902757 at each link position for lip damage, hardening or debris tracking. Where the ovality is inside limits, refit the link with the clevis pin EN768314K5 and a new retention. Where the ovality is outside limits, renew the bushing and the seal as an interim measure and record the finding for the fleet wear model. Do AMM-S-78-30-11-400-047-A to install the blocker door links. Do a reverser deployment test and record the deployment time of each half.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft with Auran 7720 or CVX-6080 engines that have not been brought to the self-lubricating bushing standard. Aircraft from MSN S01466 onward are post-modification from build. The inspection is superseded on any engine once the modification bulletin has been accomplished on both halves.
sections.material_note: No kit is required for the inspection itself. A contingency kit K7830-1009-01 containing four bushings and two seals should be held at the station where the inspection is done, since a finding cannot be deferred with the cowl open.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 4 000 flight cycles after the date of this Service Bulletin, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 4 000 flight cycles until the modification bulletin is accomplished.
